target: R.3 ‘no expert-graded subset exists’ + 1.3 ‘80 cases adjudicated by Claude’ + 2026-08-20 adoption of ‘jury-vote + entropy as Ch3/Ch4 label source’ (human anchor = those 80 + a still-pending Rehan spot-check of 10)
flaw: The entire ERIN grade/progression ontology is a closed LLM loop: the same class of model designed pathladder, judged the audit, wrote the jury prompt, and then became the training labels. High Fleiss κ (0.900) among 8 local LLMs sharing one prompt is homogenisation, not validity; related_work.md’s claim that ‘report-labels [are] validated against expert grades’ is simply false.
fix: Freeze a pathologist-adjudicated gold set (hundreds of reports, not 10) drawn before seeing jury votes; report jury vs expert κ/accuracy by class; train Ch3/Ch4 only on expert or expert-verified labels, and treat jury labels as a sensitivity arm.

target: erin_ch3_preregistration.md primary endpoint ‘current-biopsy grade classification’ with report-derived labels, and the pre-registered reading ‘Fusion benefit on primary → Ch3’s claim replicates externally at 16× scale’
flaw: The primary task is reconstructing the pathologist’s write-up of the same H&E the model sees. That is Campanella-style diagnosis-from-slide, not a replication of SWGCohort’s future-progression fusion estimand; the preregistration itself flags ‘probable label leakage: grade is itself report-derived’. A fusion win here cannot underwrite Chapter 2’s multimodal-biology claim.
fix: Make future progression (prior-timepoint clinical only, index slides strictly pre-event) the sole confirmatory endpoint; report same-slide grade as a methods/QC task, not as external replication of SWG fusion.

target: occams_v3.json hist_abmil C=0.6272 [0.5394, 0.7109], clin_cox C=0.5358 [0.4578, 0.6235], late_hist_gen Δ=−0.0396; plan note ‘shuffled controls omitted’; occams_fusion_v2 gen_only shuffled_auc=0.5806
flaw: By occams_v2_decision_tree.md, ‘signal’ requires lower 95% CI >0.55 and outcome C says if clinical-only is also null ‘no fusion conclusion of either sign can be drawn’. Histology misses that bar, stage-rich clinical is null (implausible if labels/follow-up are intact), and the control that already failed in v2 was dropped in v3 — exactly the post-hoc move the tree forbids (outcome D).
fix: Restore shuffled-label controls; audit weeks-survival and staging columns against the May 2026 clinical-only baselines; if clinical remains ~0.54, apply outcome C and remove OCCAMS from any fusion claim.

target: swg_arm.md late-mean vs CNV +0.111 AUC (0.002–0.219) but AUPRC +0.091 (−0.036–0.219); ‘[pending: paired bootstrap CI]’ for late-mean minus histology (+0.043 AUC / +0.073 AUPRC point estimates)
flaw: evaluation_protocol.md makes AUPRC the rare-class metric and the ‘question in every chapter’ the paired fusion−histology delta. The only CI that excludes zero is a barely-supported contrast against the weaker unimodal arm; the hypothesis-named contrast has no interval, and AUPRC — the pre-declared metric — is unresolved at n=150.
fix: Compute the patient-level bootstrap CI for fusion−histology on the saved OOF preds before any prose is frozen; headline AUPRC; apply a multiplicity adjustment across the seven families + co-attention, or pre-declare a single primary contrast.

target: 2026-08-21 FINDING: necessity probes n=446 TP53 AUC 0.678 / WGD 0.703 ‘Ch2 Part A’s claim must be revised from “not recoverable” to “partially recoverable at scale”’ vs evaluation_protocol.md ‘TP53 and WGD are not predictable from H&E in OCCAMS (AUC 0.48 and 0.41)’ and R.2 ‘primary claim stays OAC-only’; tcga_probe.json OAC-only TP53 AUC=0.355
flaw: The two-cohort negative was pre-committed, then reversed by pooling OAC with STAD/GEJ (a different disease) after seeing the numbers. OAC-only TP53 is anti-predictive (0.355); the ‘visibility’ result is therefore a change of population, not a scale-up of the registered claim.
fix: Keep Part A as the pre-registered OAC-only negative; report the STAD+OAC pool as a labelled exploratory extension with disease-stratified AUCs and a test of whether the signal is STAD-driven.

target: tcga_pool_fusion.json late_hist_clin C=0.6083, Δ vs hist +0.0614 [0.0273, 0.0953] while clin_cox alone is 0.6226 and hist_abmil is 0.5473 [0.5009, 0.595]; oac_subgroup_hist_c=0.6822
flaw: Fusion is sold as a benefit against a histology arm that collapses on pooling, while adding histology to clinical hurts (0.608 < 0.623). That is the flattering comparator the protocol warned against; the ‘powered’ n≈399 test actually shows clinical dominance and no genomic complementarity (late_hist_gen Δ 0.0144, CI crosses 0).
fix: Report the full triangle (hist, clin, gen, each fusion) with paired deltas vs the best unimodal; do not claim fusion benefit when fusion < clinical-only; stratify OAC vs STAD/GEJ throughout.

target: jury_corpus_analysis.json pairwise agreements ~0.90–0.98 and ‘unanimity 85.5%’ vs jury_specimen_analysis.json pairwise ~0.61–0.78; membership gated on ≥95% parse vs the Claude-adjudicated 80 (five models at 100% cancer agreement)
flaw: Near-perfect report-level agreement is inflated by the NDBE majority (5,151/6,867) and by selecting models that already cloned the Claude/pathladder rule set. When the unit is a specimen the jury fragments, so entropy is not a calibrated uncertainty measure and ‘train_eligible’ (6,867) is not a clean gold set.
fix: Re-gate models on expert agreement, not parse rate or Claude-match; report class-balanced κ and specimen-level labels; hold out all non-unanimous and all long/negation-heavy reports (disagreement_drivers.json: hedging 0.345 vs 0.116) from training.

target: encoder_sweep_preregistration.md ‘No further additions mid-sweep’ / ‘Adding encoders because results disappoint’ vs amendments that grew the grid UNI2/Virchow2/GigaPath → +H-Optimus-0 +Phikon-v2 → H-Optimus-1 (‘Grid FINAL at 6’) before any sweep result exists
flaw: The only pre-registered invariance rule (‘all encoders’ fusion deltas agree in sign with UNI2+ABMIL’) becomes cheaper to satisfy or to abandon as the grid is expanded after the protocol was frozen. This is the exact post-hoc behaviour the document forbids.
fix: Analyse the original three-encoder grid as the confirmatory sweep; treat H-Optimus/Phikon as a clearly marked add-on. Do not drop cohorts or promote a non-UNI2 encoder to the headline.

target: Phase-1 item 1.4 PORPOISE baseline still unchecked; related_work.md ‘Run as comparison arm on OCCAMS + TCGA-OAC’; 3.1 writing blocked on 1.4
flaw: Every fusion number in the digest is an in-house ABMIL/Cox variant. Without PORPOISE (or SurvPath/PathOmics) it is impossible to tell whether late-mean ‘wins’ because the pairing is real or because the published multimodal baselines were never run at these n.
fix: Run the pre-registered PORPOISE adaptation on the same frozen OCCAMS n=87 and TCGA-OAC n=65 splits and put those C-indices in the primary table before Chapter 2 is drafted.

target: OCCAMS n: planned 141 vs occams_v3 n=87 vs v2 n=84; TCGA-OAC: decision tree ‘n=78’, related_work ‘88 adenocarcinomas’, tcga_fusion_firstpass n=48, tcga_abmil n=65; ERIN progression 1,218/197 then jury v3 1,266/181; SWG 155→150

Silent row changes violate evaluation_protocol.md’s OOF contract rule.

target: pathladder negation window ‘60→130 (10 false CANCERs fixed, TCGA validation unchanged)’ after Claude review of disagreeing reports; feasibility grader ‘40/40 wrong on its side’; progression events cut ‘~30% via false CANCER calls’
flaw: The extractor was edited on the same error sample used to declare the competing grader systematically wrong, then the revised labels rebuilt the Ch3 progression cohort (197→181 progressors). That is target leakage into the label function, not an independent audit.
fix: Split a pre-touch confirmation set of reports (plus TCGA-Reports structured grade) that never informed the window change; freeze pathladder; rebuild progression v3 only after that confirmation, and pre-register the event definition.

target: SWG seven families + co-attention + three encoders; OCCAMS/TCGA multiple late fusions; necessity probes on TP53/WGD/stage/age; 0.55 ‘signal’ threshold; SWG headline AUC rather than AUPRC
flaw: Dozens of correlated tests were run and the interval that just clears zero (+0.111 AUC, lower bound 0.002) is the one written up, while AUPRC, hist-anchored deltas, OCCAMS C-index lower bounds, and clinical-vs-fusion comparisons that fail are pending, omitted, or secondary. This is metric- and contrast-shopping around a hypothesis that the pre-registrations were meant to protect.
fix: One primary contrast and metric per chapter, stated before unblinding; everything else in a single multiplicity-aware appendix; do not invoke the 0.55 rule only when it is met.
